guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not dismissing Missouri’s opener. The Tigers won 54-14, produced 562 yards and received an exceptionally efficient debut from Austin Simmons, who completed 17 of 19 passes with four touchdowns and no interceptions. That performance shows Missouri’s ability to create separation, but we are not treating one result against Arkansas-Pine Bluff as proof that the same margin should carry forward.

For us, the disagreement is less about Troy being the better team and more about how much certainty the market is assigning to Missouri. The Tigers returned only two listed defensive starters and lost 10, including six players from the front seven and three cornerbacks. Missouri’s rebuilt defense was effective in the opener, but our view leaves more room for volatility than the market price does.

The meaningful concern for our Troy position is clear: our numbers rate Missouri’s pass defense and scoring-opportunity prevention well ahead of Troy’s offense. We still expect Missouri to control much of the game. We simply think the available cushion asks Missouri to turn that control into too much separation.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Troy’s passing offense against Missouri’s pass defense. Missouri held Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 109 passing yards and a 3-of-13 conversion rate on third down, which supports the strength our model sees on that side of the ball, even if the level of competition limits what we can conclude from one game.

Troy does not need to win this matchup outright for our position to work. We need enough offensive resistance to prevent Missouri’s defensive advantage from producing repeated short possessions and a runaway margin. That is where the game is most likely to validate—or challenge—our difference with the market.

recent_game.fact: Missouri opened the 2026 season with a 54-14 home victory over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Sept. 3.
Missouri outgained Arkansas-Pine Bluff 562-198, recorded 33 first downs and converted 6-of-10 third downs and both fourth-down attempts.
Missouri led Arkansas-Pine Bluff 40-0 at halftime after outgaining the Golden Lions 376-6 in the first half.
Missouri produced 357 passing yards and 205 rushing yards against Arkansas-Pine Bluff while averaging 7.2 yards per play.

opponent_notes.fact: Missouri is scheduled to host Troy on Sept. 19 at 6 p.m. CT, with the game listed for SEC Network+.

quarterback.fact: Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons started the opener and completed 17-of-19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions.
Simmons' 89.5% completion rate and 270.4 passer rating were the highest by a quarterback in his Missouri debut.
Missouri's current depth chart lists Simmons as the starting quarterback and sophomore Matt Zollers as the backup.
Zollers completed 8-of-12 passes for 87 yards and added a five-yard rushing touchdown against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Missouri lost 2025 starting quarterback Beau Pribula and added transfers Austin Simmons and Nick Evers; Zollers returned after making three starts as a true freshman.

offensive_personnel.fact: Missouri's current first-team offensive line is LT Cayden Green, LG Tristan Wilson, C Dominick Giudice, RG Curtis Peagler and RT Luke Work.
Missouri returned five offensive starters from 2025 but lost six, including quarterback Beau Pribula, center Connor Tollison and wide receivers Kevin Coleman Jr., Marquis Johnson and Joshua Manning.
Ole Miss transfer Cayden Lee started at receiver in the opener and caught five passes for 89 yards, including a 47-yard touchdown.
Sophomore receiver Donovan Olugbode established career highs of seven receptions, 107 yards and two touchdowns in the opener.
Running back Jamal Roberts started the opener and carried 13 times for 47 yards and one touchdown.
The current depth chart lists Brett Norfleet or Jordon Harris at first-team tight end, with Jamal Roberts first at running back ahead of Xai'Shaun Edwards or Malae Fonoti.

defensive_personnel.fact: Missouri returned only two listed defensive starters from 2025 and lost 10, including six players from the defensive front seven and three cornerbacks.
Transfer linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. started 11 games for Auburn in 2025 and recorded 67 tackles.
Transfer cornerback Chris Graves Jr. appeared in 41 games over three seasons at Ole Miss and started nine games in 2025.
Missouri's current depth chart lists Nicholas Rodriguez and Robert Woodyard Jr. as the starting linebackers, with Chris Graves Jr. and Sione Laulea listed first at cornerback.
Returning edge defender Darris Smith recorded four sacks in 2025 and is listed as the current starter at the JACK position.
Linebacker Jeremiah Beasley led Missouri with seven tackles in the opener, while Jason Dowell recorded a sack.

coaching_changes.fact: Chip Lindsey joined Missouri as offensive coordinator in December 2025; he previously served as Troy's head coach from 2019-21.
Garrett Riley joined Missouri in January 2026 as quarterbacks coach after serving as Clemson's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
John Papuchis was named Missouri's special-teams coordinator and defensive assistant in January 2026 after six seasons coordinating special teams at Florida State.
Alex Atkins joined Missouri as tight ends coach in January 2026, and Chop Harbin joined as defensive line coach after five seasons at Tennessee.
Linebackers coach Derek Nicholson added co-defensive coordinator to his title before the 2026 season.

offensive_context.fact: Missouri averaged 228.3 rushing yards per game in 2025, which ranked eighth nationally and first in the SEC.
Missouri scored 31 rushing touchdowns in 2025 and rushed for three touchdowns in the 2026 opener.
Against Arkansas-Pine Bluff, Missouri converted 60% of its third downs and scored on all five red-zone possessions, with four touchdowns.

defensive_context.fact: Missouri's 2025 defense allowed 277.3 yards and 18.9 points per game, including 103.8 rushing yards and 173.5 passing yards per game.
Missouri held Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 198 total yards, including 89 rushing and 109 passing, and a 3-of-13 third-down conversion rate.
Missouri's defense forced five three-and-outs against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

special_teams.fact: Missouri's current depth chart lists Brunno Reus as the punter, kickoff specialist and holder, Blake Craig as the placekicker, and DaMarion Fowlkes as the primary punt and kickoff returner.
Craig made a 32-yard field goal and all seven extra-point attempts in the season opener.
Fowlkes returned a punt 23 yards against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

other_relevant.fact: Missouri has won 24 consecutive home games against non-SEC opponents, a streak dating to Oct. 21, 2017.
Missouri has won 12 consecutive home night games and 14 consecutive regular-season night games overall.
Missouri is 19-2 in regular-season nonconference games under head coach Eli Drinkwitz.
